page: Vultr voc-c-16c-32gb-300s-amd is an Optimized Cloud Compute server powered by an x86_64 AMD EPYC processor. It features 16 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 8 physical cores with 2 threads per core, operating at a base clock speed of 2.0 GHz. The processor includes 16 MB of L3 cache and supports instruction sets such as AVX, AES, SHA_NI, and BMI2. The system is equipped with 32.0 GB of system memory, providing a resource density of 2.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. Local storage is provided by a 300 GB NVMe SSD, and the server includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. No GPU hardware is present.

Benchmark evaluations indicate strong single-core performance, with stress-ng and Geekbench single-core scores placing in the top 25% of tested systems. Multi-core performance, measured via stress-ng and Geekbench multi-core tests, falls within the middle 50% average tier. Memory bandwidth tests for both cached small blocks and uncached large blocks also demonstrate average performance, with uncached read speeds reaching 149.65 GB/sec and write speeds at 71.14 GB/sec. In specialized workloads, the server exhibits top-tier performance in text generation for small language models, and strong performance in text generation for medium models, alongside strong image and text processing capabilities.

Given its 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio and dedicated CPU allocation, this server offers a compute-focused resource profile. It provides a balanced tradeoff for workloads that require dedicated CPU execution without the high memory overhead of general-purpose instances, making it a qualitatively cost-efficient option for compute-bound tasks. The hardware configuration and benchmark results make it suitable for workloads such as web serving, software compilation, medium-scale database operations, and CPU-based machine learning inference for small to medium models.
